header:
Date: 2027-12-06 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Claire Johnson (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Morales (Redwood CSM); Marta Li (Velaris CTO), Emilio Santos (Velaris DevOps), Priya Nair (Velaris SRE), Jonah Reed (Velaris Product)
summary: Initial reliability intake focused on graceful degradation, partial responses (95% vs 100% traffic), multi-region routing, and SLA language. Velaris has hybrid infra with EU data residency needs and wants canary + circuit-breaker policies. Key asks: explicit fallback policy options, costs/latency tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated vs private, SOC2 + KMS details, and a small perf benchmark run with sample traffic.
topics: fallback policies and variants (model downgrade, rate-limiting, cached responses)
multi-region routing vs single-region dedicated pools
benchmarking ask and next-step pilot setup
transcript:
[00:00] Claire: Hey everyone, thanks for making time — Claire from Redwood. Quick intro; I'll hand to Ravi for the deep bits later.
[00:07] Marta: Hi, thanks. We're hoping to map options for keeping our assistant available during partial outages, like we can't have full-throttle but need soft failures.
[00:14] Ravi: Great, that's what we do. When you say soft failures do you mean partial responses, degraded model outputs, cached answers, or synthetic fallbacks?
[00:21] Marta: All of the above. For payments flows we want anything that avoids a hard 500. Priya, you want to add?
[00:26] Priya: Yeah, our SRE playbook says no full outage for >30s for customer-facing endpoints. If the LLM backend goes slow we either want: 1) fast degraded answer from a smaller model, or 2) a short text stub 'system busy, try again' plus cached disclaimers.
[00:41] Emilio: Also important: we run EU weighted traffic for residency; we can't route EU PII to US without consent. So multi-region routing is a must.
[00:50] Ravi: Cool. On Redwood side we support a few levers: model variant fallback (bigger -> smaller quantized), region-aware routing policies, and prefix/K-V cache to surface previous responses. We also have circuit breakers and automatic rate-limits per token to cap cost during storms.
[01:05] Jonah: Is the prefix cache per tenant or global? Because in our product the same prompt can come from different customers and we need per-tenant isolation.
[01:12] Ravi: Per-tenant. Cache keys are scoped to customer IDs. Small caveat — if you want extremely strict on-disk separation you'd be looking at Private deployment. Hosted supports strong logical isolation, encryption at rest with customer-specific keys via KMS.
[01:27] Marta: Quick question on SLAs: we saw your baseline hosted SLOs but what does Redwood guarantee for partial degradation? Like, can we define an SLO that says 99.5% 'meaningful' responses with 300ms token median?
[01:38] Claire: We typically offer target SLOs for latency and availability. For Hosted we publish 99.9% availability for API control-plane and a latency band per-model. For enterprise Dedicated we can commit stronger numeric SLOs and fallbacks as contractual items — e.g., guaranteed routing to dedicated pool with X failover time. For Private, we defer to your infra but provide the runtime and ops guidance.
[01:57] Priya: So for Dedicated, you can guarantee fallback response within a specific window if a zone fails?
[02:03] Ravi: Yes. For dedicated pools deployed multi-region we can configure active-passive or active-active. Active-active gives near-instant failover; active-passive means a short rehydration time for KV caches. Also we can route a proportion of traffic to a cheaper model when a region is waxed over to preserve latency. Sorry — when a region is degraded.
[02:22] Emilio: Rehydration time — how bad is it? If KV cache cold-start means 5s tails that's not acceptable for our checkout flow.
[02:29] Ravi: Cold-start depends on model size and KV volume. For large models with big KV state it can be several seconds. We mitigate with warm-standby replicas and cross-region KV replication, but that increases inter-region egress and cost. So it's a tradeoff.
[02:45] Marta: Cost is a big factor. Can you show us cost/latency curves for hosted vs dedicated vs private for a 2M token/month workload with 90/10 peak distribution?
[02:55] Claire: We'll send a concise cost baseline spreadsheet — it includes default batching, quantization profiles, and expected latency bands per model family. We'll also outline where autoscale and burst costs enter.
[03:06] Jonah: On the fallback policies — do you have the ability to do 'graceful degrade to summary mode' where, instead of full generation, system returns a short extractive summary from cached docs?
[03:15] Ravi: We don't implement ground-truth extractive summarization by default, but we support custom tool calls and can route to a reranker/extractive model path as a fallback. Some customers set up a hybrid where vectordb + small model gives extractive fallback.
[03:30] Priya: Hmm. We have an internal vectordb for retention — would Redwood be able to call our vector endpoint in a Private setup?
[03:36] Claire: Yes, Private allows network integration, private endpoints, and you can keep the vectordb inside your VPC. Hosted can call external numbered endpoints but you need network peering for PII-sensitive flows.
[03:49] Emilio: About security: we need SOC2 Type II, ISO, audit logs, and bring-your-own-key KMS. Can you confirm those?
[03:57] Claire: We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO plans; we provide audit logs and RBAC. BYOK is supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted supports customer-key encryption using a managed KMS integration. I'll attach the security deck and the SOC2 cert.
[04:12] Marta: Great. A practical concern: our acceptance criteria for pilot is that during a simulated region outage, customer-facing flows degrade gracefully with under 1.0% error rate and median latency increase under 2x. Is that reasonable to test?
[04:25] Ravi: Yes, we can design a chaos simulation. In a Dedicated pilot we can spin a reserve region and run failover tests. For Hosted we'll need to simulate capacity constraints and test model fallbacks. The 1.0% error target is achievable if you accept smaller-model degradation and caching.
[04:40] Claire: On legal side — do you have procurement timelines? That helps us choose Hosted pilot vs Dedicated proof-of-concept.
[04:46] Marta: Procurement's about 6–8 weeks for enterprise contracts. We prefer to start a Hosted pilot while procurement runs for Dedicated.
[04:53] Jonah: Are there built-in rollout policies for canaries and A/B? We want to test the fallback in a staged way.
[04:59] Ravi: Yes — canary traffic splits, A/B experiments, and automatic rollback triggers based on error rate, latency, and quality regressions. We also surface prompt-level regressions via Redwood Optimize.
[05:11] Priya: One more operational nit: do you expose metrics at token-level for cost attribution so we can tie specific routes to business metrics?
[05:18] Claire: Yes, console exposes token-level cost, latency per-route, and per-model breakdowns. You can export to your monitoring stack.
[05:25] Marta: Ok, small clarification — when you say 'smaller model' fallback, how do you ensure output quality doesn't introduce safety/reg compliance issues? For legal/regarded content we need deterministic decline rather than hallucinated short answers.
[05:38] Ravi: Good question. We recommend fail-close behaviour for regulated prompts — return an error or a templated decline message. For non-regulated UX flows, degraded model or extractive fallbacks are acceptable. We can attach policy tags to routes so certain prompts always use 'fail-close'.
[05:53] Emilio: On-network topology — if we do Dedicated but in our EU region only, can you still provide global failover to US region while honouring data residency? We can't send PII out of EU.
tail_transcript:
[06:06] Ravi: You'd need a tiered approach: EU-only pool for PII flows and a separate global pool for non-PII. Routing policy would mark certain routes 'EU-only' and those would never cross region. For other routes we can failover globally.
[06:20] Marta: Good — that'll be our approach.
[06:23] Claire: Recap — action items: we'll send SOC2/security deck, cost baseline, and a pilot proposal with a chaos test plan. Ravi will prep the perf questionnaire. You'll share traffic histograms.
[06:34] Priya: Timeline: if we get the security docs by 12/08 we can schedule the tech deep dive week of 12/13.
[06:39] Claire: Perfect — thanks everyone. We'll follow up today with links: security deck (link), cost baseline (sheet link), and a short pilot proposal.
[06:46] Marta: Thanks all.
[06:48] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional misheard words: 'KV' appears as 'K-V' or 'k v', 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes heard as 'Redwood dedicate' in auto-transcript. There were a few overlaps, speaker labels verified against calendar but not perfect. Shared artifacts referenced: security deck (note: /redwood/security/soc2.pdf), benchmark spreadsheet (note: /redwood/pilot/velaris-benchmark.xlsx), pilot proposal (note: /redwood/pilot/velaris-proposal.md).
conclusion: Velaris is aligned to run a Hosted pilot in parallel with procurement for Dedicated. Key technical concerns: guaranteed graceful degradation paths, EU data residency for PII, BYOK/KMS, and measurable SLOs for partial-response behavior. Next step: Redwood to share security + cost artifacts and schedule a technical deep dive week of 2027-12-13.
